title: Expected-Path Retrieval Diagnose Contract
summary: Explain why one canonical repository-relative path was returned, ranked out, excluded, unpublished, unmatched, or absent without scanning the full generated corpus.

release.compatibility: Shin v1.25 requires an explicit generator-v17 rebuild for corrected authority semantics. No compatibility reader or implicit migration is retained.

rules: absolute paths, dot segments, parent traversal, and non-canonical spelling are rejected
the raw spelling is validated before any root join
the path is interpreted only within the configured profile and repository root

execution.session: One RetrievalSession pins the generated publication, freshness proof, and manifest for the complete command.
execution.primaryRetrieval: The normal brief request determines whether the expected path is returned and its global unique-path rank.

budgetProbe.purpose: Observe whether a path appears with expanded output budgets. This is not proof that the original route admitted it or that only global ranking excluded it.
budgetProbe.execution: executed=false and null probe result fields mean the normal request already returned the path; no expanded request was run.
budgetProbe.route: Report expanded retrieval_mode, candidate_rows and required_group_matches. route_changed compares the reported route names; false is not proof of identical candidate sets or planner decisions.

sparsePathProbe.algorithm: Binary-search each path-sorted row-offset index, then inspect only the contiguous rows for the expected path.
sparsePathProbe.failureRule: Malformed, non-contiguous, oversized, or incomplete generated row indexes fail closed as index-corrupt.

execution.publicationState: Document and source-fact publication state is read from the pinned active manifest, not inferred from current source enumeration.
execution.outputBoundary: The result is built under the shared lock and emitted after the retrieval session is destroyed.

ranking.returnedPathRank: One-based unique path rank in the normal requested brief result, or null.
ranking.rankTable: retrieval.ranked_paths is the same ordered path table emitted by brief and eval for identical profile, snapshot, query, and limits.

resultSemantics.ok: True only when the expected path is present in the normal requested result.
resultSemantics.soft: Without --strict an unmet expectation returns exit 0 with ok=false for inspection.
resultSemantics.strict: With --strict an unmet expectation returns exit 1 with the same shin.diagnose.v1 document.
resultSemantics.source: Reports current regular-file existence, document policy, source-fact configuration, and pinned publication state.
resultSemantics.indexed_rows: Reports typed row counts, sparse probe completeness, and actual rows examined.
resultSemantics.matching: Reports the best path-local group match, score, line, record type, evidence kind, verification level, fields, and group indices.
resultSemantics.retrieval: Reports strict, relaxed, or planned mode, candidate work, coverage, rank table, and planner selection.

verification: expanded request changes relaxed retrieval to document planning without claiming global rank-out
already returned path does not claim an executed expanded probe
authorityBoundary: Diagnose explains deterministic retrieval mechanics. It does not declare a source correct, current in product meaning, or more authoritative than its repository contract.
nonGoals: no scoring mutation or automatic profile tuning
